Article Title: Supeme Court to Mahua: Freedom fighters faced bullets, you fear eggs
Article Text:
Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan , appearing for the MP, contended before the bench that she should be permitted to appear before the investigation officer through video conferencing.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed TMC MP Mahua Moitra 's plea seeking permission to appear virtually before police in a case against her for uploading a provocative post on Facebook.As the MP took the ground that she will be attacked by a mob if she physically went there and eggs may be thrown at her, a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said, "You are an MP? Having taken the plunge into politics, you fear eggs? When our freedom fighters have taken bullets on their chest? These are applications that should not come before this court at all. "Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for the MP, contended before the bench that she should be permitted to appear before the investigation officer through video conferencing."Why virtually? Because you are an MP?" the court asked.
Article Summary: TMC MP Mahua Moitra's plea seeking permission to appear virtually before police in a case against her for uploading a provocative post on Facebook. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for the MP, contended before the bench that she should be permitted to appear before the investigation officer through video conferencing.

Article Title: Supreme Court dismisses Bofors appeal, 4-decade-old case closed
Article Text:
Justice RS Sodhi of Delhi high court had quashed all charges against the Hinduja brothers and AB Bofors, holding that the prosecution failed to provide admissible, reliable evidence

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has dismissed an appeal challenging a 2005 Delhi HC judgement that had quashed criminal proceedings in the Bofors pay-off case , bringing to an end a four-decade-old politically sensitive case.A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran rejected the appeal filed by advocate Ajay K Agrawal, who pleaded for adjournment of the hearing.During the brief hearing, Agrawal requested four weeks to delete the names of parties who have died during the pendency of the case - Srichand P Hinduja and Gopichand P Hinduja. Prakash P Hinduja, who is the Europe chairman of the Hinduja Group, remains a respondent in the case. SC, however, refused to grant any further time to prolong the 2018 matter. "No question of adjournment. It is a 2018 matter," the bench said, before dismissing the appeal.Agrawal, who contested the 2014 Lok Sabha election from Rae Bareli against the then Congress president Sonia Gandhi, filed the appeal after CBI did not challenge the high court order due to the denial of permission by the then UPA govt to file an appeal before the Supreme Court.Justice RS Sodhi of Delhi high court had quashed all charges against the Hinduja brothers and AB Bofors, holding that the prosecution failed to provide admissible, reliable evidence linking the accused to the alleged kickbacks. As the CBI did not file a timely appeal against the high court order, Agrawal filed a third-party petition before the top court challenging the quashing of charges.
Article Summary: A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran rejected the appeal filed by advocate Ajay K Agrawal. Justice RS Sodhi of Delhi high court had quashed all charges against the Hinduja brothers and AB Bofors, holding that the prosecution failed to provide admissible, reliable evidence.

Article Title: 'Hands off Jantar Mantar!' CJP says 'won't tolerate' bid to take away protest site after HC poser
Article Text:
CJP reacts to HC hearing on Jantar Mantar as the protest venue site

'Why should the city be put to ransom unnecessarily': Delhi HC

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party spokesperson Saurav Das on Friday defended Jantar Mantar as Delhi's key protest venue after the Delhi HC questioned whether demonstrations should continue in the heart of the capital.In a post on X, Das wrote, "HANDS OFF our Jantar Mantar!" He alleged that after public protests were no longer allowed at India Gate, any move to shift demonstrations away from Jantar Mantar would curtail citizens' democratic rights."Before trying to take away our protest site, tell us if you will designate the India Gate where we can exercise our fundamental right to peacefully protest. You took away the India Gate.We will not tolerate taking away of OUR Jantar Mantar too!" he said.Also read: Jantar Mantar 'terror plot' row: Amritsar top cop Gurpreet Bhullar shunted; BJP cries foul Das's remarks came after Justice Amit Mahajan, while hearing a petition seeking permission to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar, orally observed that protests should not inconvenience the city and asked, "Why should the city be put to ransom unnecessarily?"The court directed Delhi Police to decide the petitioner's request by Saturday but did not order whether permission should be granted or denied.The issue of whether Jantar Mantar should remain Delhi's designated protest site is also pending before the Supreme Court, which is examining a plea seeking an alternative venue for demonstrations in the national capital.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party spokesperson Saurav Das defended Jantar Mantar as Delhi's key protest venue. Delhi HC questioned whether demonstrations should continue in the heart of the capital. Justice Amit Mahajan orally observed that protests should not inconvenience the city and asked, "Why should the city be put to ransom unnecessarily?"

Article Title: Sukhbir Singh Badal meets PM Modi, fuels BJP-SAD alliance buzz ahead of Punjab polls next year
Article Text:
Badal-PM Modi meet sparked SAD-BJP alliance buzz

NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) chief Sukhbir Singh Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Parliament on Friday. The meeting has sparked buzz over whether the BJP and the SAD are preparing to turn the page on years of political estrangement ahead of the Punjab assembly elections due early next year.For both the BJP and the SAD, the timing is significant. Once the state's dominant political combine, the two parties have spent the past several years on the margins of Punjab politics, watching their traditional support base shrink while Kejriwal-led Aam Aadmi Party gradually emerged as the state's principal political force.The BJP-SAD who were allies for over two decades, parted ways in September 2020 after the Akali Dal walked out of the NDA , with much credits to Centre's three farm laws. The legislation triggered massive protests across Punjab and countrywide and became a political flashpoint.However, even after PM Modi-led government repealed the laws in 2021, relations between the two allies remained strained.Also read: Can BJP crack Punjab? Inside its strategy to challenge AAP and Congress in 2027 In the 2022 Punjab assembly elections, voters not only rejected the Congress, which was crippled by the Amarinder Singh-Navjot Singh Sidhu power struggle, but also delivered a crushing verdict against both the BJP and the SAD.Contesting separately, the BJP won just two seats while the Akali Dal managed only three in the 117-member assembly.Instead, Punjab handed Kejriwal's AAP a historic mandate. The party stormed to power for the first time in its second attempt, with Bhagwant Mann becoming chief minister, recording a dramatic shift in the Sikh-majority state.Against this backdrop, the Modi-Badal meeting in Parliament assumes greater political significance. While neither side has officially indicated that an alliance is on the cards, the interaction is likely to intensify discussions over whether the estranged partners can rebuild their relationship before Punjab votes next year.
Article Summary: Badal-PM Modi meet sparked SAD-BJP alliance buzz. The meeting has sparked buzz over whether the BJP and the SAD are preparing to turn the page on years of political estrangement ahead of the Punjab assembly elections due early next year.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi slams BJP over NEET protest crackdown, says students were forced to apologise
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi slams BJP over NEET crackdown

NEW DELHI: Standing with a group of youngsters who faced police action during the NEET protests , Congress leader Rahul Gandhi Wednesday said the ruling party is sending goons to the homes of students and forcing them to apologise, after which those apologies are being accepted by the PM.“There is no question of the youngsters apologising… I am very proud of them and what thousands of them did… They defended the Constitution and protected the idea of India and India’s future,” Rahul said.The Congress leader held a “freewheeling” discussion at his residence with a group of youngsters who participated in the protests at Jantar Mantar and other parts of the country. It included Riya Ahir whose photo went viral after she stood in front of a police van in Mumbai and Muskan Sharma who was victim of a cop “jabbing a baton into her buttocks” at Jantar Mantar on July 20. Farah Naaz alleged that in police detention, she faced communal barbs with a cop even calling her “anti-national”. Muskan said she was being assumed to be a Muslim which makes an Indian a “fair game”, even clarifying that she is a Hindu. Nutan Toppo said a pellet gun was fired at her.The leader of opposition’s decision to meet the youngsters to 10, Janpath, for a chat further upped the ante in the “BJP vs opposition” confrontation that has jammed the ongoing monsoon session of parliament.Continuing its aggression, a large contingent of opposition MPs marched inside the Parliament complex to protest the “absence of Amit Shah from parliament” and “Ayodhya donation scam”. The group included Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Dimple Yadav, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Dharmendra Yadav, Supriya Sule, NK Premachandran, Sagarika Ghose, Amar Singh, Chowdry Mohd Ramzan, John Brittas, Sandosh Kumar, Naseer Hussain, K Radhakrishnan.Rahul held a placard with a face riddled with pellet gun injuries and a question “who gave the order?” The members also sought statehood for J&K.Addressing the media with the youngsters, Rahul said, “They are so young and standing before the media. But the prime minister and the home minister have no courage to stand before the press."He attacked home minister Amit Shah by saying that he is responsible for the crackdown on youngsters but “he does not have the decency to come to the Parliament, and the courage to comment on what happened.”Rahul took a jibe at PM Narendra Modi for saying that he has forgiven the students.
Article Summary: The Congress leader held a “freewheeling’ discussion at his residence with a group of youngsters who participated in the protests at Jantar Mantar and other parts of the country. The group included Riya Ahir whose photo went viral after she stood in front of a police van in Mumbai and Muskan Sharma who was victim of a cop “jabbing a baton into her buttocks”

Article Title: 3 rebel TMC MPs to meet Prime Minister today
Article Text:
Three minority breakaway Trinamool Congress MPs will meet PM Modi over breakfast on Friday

Article Title: AAP protests over ‘health scam’, BJP seeks action against ‘illegal’ small hotels
Article Text:
TOI





New Delhi: The first day of the assembly’s monsoon session witnessed a political slugfest Friday, with AAP seeking a debate on an alleged Rs 650-crore health scam and also protesting over it. Meanwhile, BJP MLA Harish Khurana sought a crackdown on small hotels allegedly operating illegally in residential areas.The chief whip of opposition AAP, Sanjeev Jha, said five party MLAs were marshalled out after they demanded a discussion on the “Rs 650-crore health scam” regarding the procurement of medicines and medical equipment. “BJP govt refused to allow a debate on the issue and was evading accountability by convening two consecutive assembly sessions without Question Hour,” Jha said. “Govt is neither allowing Question Hour nor permitting a discussion on this issue. Instead, we were marshalled out merely for standing up and making this demand,” he alleged.AAP MLAs protested on the assembly premises and demanded the health minister’s resignation.Minister Parvesh Verma said the opposition had a problem because BJP govt had initiated the process of giving Rs 2,500 monthly financial assistance to women.“In five years (during AAP govt), 74 sittings of the assembly were held, but Question Hour was there only during nine of them. In 2024, there was not a single Question Hour,” Verma claimed.In the meantime, Khurana said many small hotels were functioning without licences and in violation of building bye-laws, master plan and fire safety norms. Raising the issue during a special mention under Rule 280, the Moti Nagar MLA said such establishments were posing risks to residents’ safety, particularly women and children, besides affecting law and order, parking, sanitation and the peace of residential colonies.He urged govt to conduct a joint enforcement drive and direct district magistrates to identify and act against such violators.Hitting out at AAP over the absence of leader of the opposition Atishi and senior MLA Gopal Rai at the sitting, Delhi BJP spokesperson Praveen Shankar Kapoor said, “The absence of Atishi and Gopal Rai shows AAP’s seriousness towards constitutional institutions and democratic processes. It is unfortunate that Atishi, who enjoys the privileges provided through the taxpayers’ money, is occupied with welcoming Arvind Kejriwal in Goa, while Rai has spent months campaigning in Gujarat.”No response was available from AAP despitereaching out to it.
Article Summary: The first day of the assembly’s monsoon session witnessed a political slugfest Friday. AAP seeking a debate on an alleged Rs 650-crore health scam and also protesting over it. Meanwhile, BJP MLA Harish Khurana sought a crackdown on small hotels allegedly operating illegally in residential areas.

Article Title: HC seeks EC response on SIR petition by Cong
Article Text: New Delhi: Delhi High Court Friday sought the Election Commission (EC)’s stand on a plea by Delhi Pradesh Congress Committee (DPCC) president Devender Yadav claiming gaps in the rollout of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in the city.The petition by Yadav, and the chairman, booth management committee of DPCC, assailed the mandate to booth level agents (BLAs) of political parties to give a personal undertaking certifying that they have personally verified all details in the enumeration forms.Justice Amit Bansal asked the Election Commission to file its response to the plea and listed it for hearing on Aug 12.The plea argues that neither the Representation of the People Act nor the Registration of Electors Rules contain any provision empowering the Election Commission to ask representatives of political parties to give such an undertaking.“The requirement of a personal undertaking from BLAs is directly contrary to the statutory scheme of verification prescribed under Section 23 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, which mandates that the inclusion of any name in the electoral roll shall be made by the electoral registration officer, and only after ‘proper verification of facts in such manner as may be prescribed’,” the petition said.“The prescribed manner of verification under the rules is to be conducted by statutory officers, not by private individuals or party representatives.The imposition of an undertaking of personal verification upon BLAs amounts to an unlawful delegation of a statutory function to private actors,” the plea said.The petitioners were represented by senior advocate Sakal Bhushan and advocates Sunil Kumar and Prateek Sinha.They have sought a direction to set aside the SIR guidelines that require such a personal undertaking by booth-level agents.It also sought a direction to the EC to provide printed and soft copies of the 2022 electoral rolls of 2002 and the ‘frozen photo electoral roll’ for Delhi to enable the petitioners’ BLAs to effectively assist in the SIR.
Article Summary: Delhi Pradesh Congress Committee (DPCC) president Devender Yadav claimed gaps in the rollout of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in the city. The petition by Yadav, and the chairman, booth management committee of DPCC, assailed the mandate to booth level agents (BLAs) of political parties.

Article Title: Ahead of Union cabinet reshuffle, Shinde meets PM
Article Text:

Mumbai: Political circles were once again rife with speculation after DCM Eknath Shinde visited Delhi on Friday and met PM Narendra Modi in Parliament. This was Shinde’s first meeting with PM Modi after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led student protests and came ahead of the possible Union Cabinet reshuffle and the introduction of the delimitation bill in Parliament. The functionary said PM Modi also met 6 Sena MPs who joined Shinde recently from Sena (UBT) and discussed issues related to their constituencies over breakfast on Friday. Govt is ready to discuss; govt is with the youth, and it was by respecting and honouring the youth that Dharmendra Pradhan resigned. Article Title: Pvt vehicles banned in an around CPR Hospital till Sunday afternoon
Article Text:
Private vehicles banned in CPR Hospital

Kolhapur

:





Private vehicles have been banned in and around Chhatrapati Pramila Raje (CPR) civil hospital from Friday afternoon until Sunday afternoon, as several development works within the hospital premises are set to be inaugurated in the presence of chief minister Devendra Fadnavis , deputy chief ministers and other ministers.The hospital dean issued a notification clarifying that the restrictions will not apply to emergency vehicles, and that adequate precautions have been taken to avoid any inconvenience to patients and their relatives.The hospital is located along the busy Bhausingji Road which is home to several govt establishments. Directly opposite the hospital stands the building of the Bombay High Court’s Kolhapur bench.Though the ban of private vehicles on paper was supposed to start from 12pm, the security deployment at the hospital started the enforcement from morning which caught the visitors by surprise.As a result, the road got congested and the traffic department had to deploy additional staff to regulate movement of vehicles.“The restrictions have been placed for security reasons. It is approved by the police department. The visitors are requested to cooperate,” CPR Hospital dean Dr Sadanand Bhise said.
Article Summary: Private vehicles have been banned in and around Chhatrapati Pramila Raje (CPR) civil hospital from Friday afternoon until Sunday afternoon. Several development works within the hospital premises are set to be inaugurated in the presence of chief minister Devendra Fadnavis.

Article Title: Bombay high court grants bail to Solapur BJP corporator in MNS politician murder case
Article Text:
Police personnel took BJP Solapur corporator Shalan Shinde from jail to a polling booth to cast her vote for the recent MLC election

Kolhapur:





The Bombay high court’s Kolhapur bench has granted bail to Solapur Municipal Corporation’s BJP corporator Shalan Shankar Shinde, who is one of the accused in the murder of Maharashtra Navnirman Sena students’ wing city chief Balasaheb Sarwade earlier this year.Shinde was arrested along with seven others, including her husband, sons, sister and supporters, following Sarwade’s murder on Jan 2. According to the prosecution, Sarwade had filed his nomination for the Solapur Municipal Corporation elections and was allegedly pressured to withdraw it. Though he withdrew his candidature, he allegedly confronted the Shinde family over the treatment meted out to his relatives shortly before he was killed.Shinde subsequently won the civic election while in judicial custody and had recently been permitted to cast her vote in the MLC election. After her sister, Sharda Shinde, secured bail, Shalan Shinde approached the high court seeking regular bail. The plea was opposed by the prosecution and by Bajirao Pandurang Sarwade, brother of the deceased.“The applicant is a prominent resident of the area and is a sitting corporator.The applicant has deep roots in the society and is not a flight risk. The applicant also does not have criminal antecedents. The applicant is ready to abide by any condition that may be imposed by this court. The applicant may, therefore, be released on bail,” Shinde’s counsel argued before the court, according to the Aug 4 order.Opposing the plea, the prosecution and intervenor argued that Shinde was directly named in the FIR and had an active role in the crime.“The applicant is directly named in the FIR. The applicant is also attributed the role of throwing the chili powder. The applicant is also attributed exhortation to the other accused persons to kill deceased Balasaheb Sarwade... The offence is serious in nature. As the applicant is a sitting corporator, there is every likelihood that the applicant, if released on bail, may influence the witnesses,” they submitted.Granting bail, Justice Mehroz K Pathan noted discrepancies in eyewitness accounts and the limited role attributed to Shinde in the FIR.“The apprehensions of the learned APP as well as the learned counsel for the complainant can be taken care of by imposing stringent conditions upon the applicant. The applicant is a woman and has a family to look after. The investigation is complete and the chargesheet is filed. No fruitful purpose would be served by keeping the woman behind bars. Taking into consideration the limited role attributed to the applicant in the FIR and the material discrepancy, occurring in the statements of the eye witnesses, I am inclined to exercise discretion under section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023,” stated Justice Pathan before allowing the bail application and imposing conditions such as personal bond of Rs 1 lakh, showing up at police station once in two months and not entering the jurisdiction of the Jail Road police station untill framing of charges, except when required to mark her attendance.
Article Summary: Shalan Shankar Shinde is one of the accused in the murder of Maharashtra Navnirman Sena students’ wing city chief Balasaheb Sarwade earlier this year. She was arrested along with seven others, including her husband, sons, sister and supporters.

Article Title: Former BJP state general secretary arrested in Atrocities Act case
Article Text:
The case stems from an audio clip that went viral on social media last month

Nashik:





Former BJP state general secretary Vijay Chaudhary was arrested on Thursday in connection with a case registered against him under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.The case stems from an audio clip that went viral on social media last month, in which Chaudhary was allegedly heard making objectionable and casteist remarks against former Nandurbar MP Heena Gavit. Based on a complaint, the Nandurbar city police registered an FIR against him on July 28 under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for outraging modesty and sections of the Atrocities Act.Nandurbar sub-divisional police officer Hanumant Gaikwad said Chaudhary had been evading arrest since the FIR was filed. Acting on a tip-off, the local crime branch tracked him to a location on Thursday, detained him and handed him over to the investigating team.Chaudhary was arrested later that night and produced before a court, which remanded him to police custody till Aug 10. Gaikwad said, “Investigators will collect Chaudhary’s voice sample and send it for forensic analysis to verify whether it matches the voice heard in the viral audio clip.We will also probe the origin and circulation of the recording to determine who made it public.”Following the registration of the FIR, Chaudhary resigned from his post as BJP’s North Maharashtra coordinator.In a separate development, the Akkalkuwa police registered another case against Chaudhary on Aug 4 based on a complaint filed by Giridhar Dharma Padvi, secretary of the Akhil Bharatiya Adivasi Mahasangh. The complaint alleges that Chaudhary made derogatory and defamatory remarks about MLA Amshya Padvi, a member of the Bhil Scheduled Tribe community, during a phone conversation.
Article Summary: Vijay Chaudhary was arrested on Thursday in connection with a case registered against him under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The case stems from an audio clip that went viral on social media last month.

Article Title: Man posing as police officer robs four workers of mobile phones; arrested
Article Text:
Chennai:





Police arrested a 26-year-old man for posing as a police officer and robbing four private company employees of three expensive mobile phones at knifepoint in Singaperumal Koil in Chengalpet district.Police identified the accused as Dhanush , 26, of Sasthirambakkam near Singaperumal Koil. The stolen mobile phones, valued at about ₹1 lakh, were recovered from him. He was produced before a magistrate’s court in Chengalpet and remanded in judicial custody on Thursday. Mohan Kumar , 21, Ranjith Kumar and two other employees from Nagapattinam district were staying in a rented house in Thirutheri near Singaperumal Koil while working for a private company, police said. Late at night, Dhanush knocked on the door, identified himself as a police officer and claimed he had received information that ganja was being stored inside the house. He entered the premises and conducted a search.Police said the accused then took a knife from the kitchen, held it to Ranjith Kumar’s neck, threatened the occupants and robbed them of three high-end mobile phones. He fled immediately after the robbery.Based on a complaint lodged by Mohan Kumar, Singaperumal Koil police registered a case and examined CCTV footage from the neighbourhood. The footage helped investigators identify and trace the accused.Police said Dhanush had more than 10 criminal cases registered against him at stations including Maraimalai Nagar and Palur.
Article Summary: Police identified the accused as Dhanush, 26, of Sasthirambakkam near Singaperumal Koil. The stolen mobile phones, valued at about ₹1 lakh, were recovered from him. He was produced before a magistrate’s court in Chengalpet and remanded in judicial custody.

Article Title: Prepared to face humiliation for Tamil Nadu in Cauvery issue, says Vijay
Article Text:
Prepared to face humiliation for Tamil Nadu in Cauvery issue, says Vijay

Chennai:





Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Friday defended his attempt to travel to Bengaluru over the Cauvery river dispute, stating that if rival countries could hold talks to resolve disputes, so could two neighbouring states. Vijay said he is prepared to face “humiliation for the sake of Tamil Nadu” even if there’s a setback at the dialogue table. The debate also turned into political sparring between Vijay and the leader of the opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin Breaking his silence over the proposed visit, which was shelved after Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar said the situation was not conducive for talks, Vijay said the outreach for direct talks was his idea. He was responding to Udhayanidhi, who alleged that there was a lack of transparency on the part of TN govt while Karnataka CM had spoken about the dialogue plan.Replying to a special calling-attention motion on the Cauvery dispute and Mekedatu dam row, CM Vijay said he sees dialogue as a positive step towards resolving the problem and added that he had “no intention to play politics” over the issue.Vijay said his administration would never compromise on Tamil Nadu ’s riparian rights, even as it pursues legal and political remedies. He recalled that following a unanimous assembly resolution opposing the dam, the state govt wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi .Vijay said that after realising the Union Minister of State for Jal Shakti had “not presented the full facts” about the Mekedatu dam project in Parliament, his govt wrote to PM Modi again, citing Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal’s final order and the Supreme Court judgment.The debate quickly turned into a political face-off between Vijay and Udhayanidhi Stalin. Udhayanidhi questioned the govt’s handling of the Cauvery crisis and demanded an all-party meeting.Vijay responded that his govt had already announced a special kuruvai package for farmers. “A party that claims to be political masterminds should read newspapers to know what was happening in the state,’’ he said.The jab drew an immediate counter from Udhayanidhi. “What we are asking for is drought relief, while what the govt has given was special kuruvai package. First, you should understand the difference between the two,’’ he said.“So, reading newspapers is not enough; you should interact with farmers to know ground reality,’’ Udhayanidhi said in a sharp retort.AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami too demanded that the govt to convene an all-party meeting and take necessary measures to safeguard Tamil Nadu’s water rights.
Article Summary: Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay defended his attempt to travel to Bengaluru over the Cauvery river dispute. Vijay said he is prepared to face “humiliation for the sake of Tamil Nadu’ even if there’s a setback at the dialogue table. The debate turned into political sparring between Vijay and the leader of the opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin.

Article Title: Madras HC summons vigilance officer over failure to imprison convicted VAO
Article Text:
Madras HC summons vigilance officer over failure to imprison convicted VAO





Madurai: Madras high court has summoned the chief vigilance commissioner to explain the action taken against an investigation officer of the DVAC for failing to secure a former village administrative officer (VAO) in Madurai district, who was convicted in a case for accepting a bribe in 2008.The case of the prosecution is that P T M Pandiarajan was working as the VAO of Nadumuthalaikulam village in Madurai district. He was also in-charge of Panniyan, Kullaneri and Kannanur villages. In 2008, a person from Kannanur village approached Pandiarajan seeking an adangal copy of his land for obtaining a loan. Since Pandiarajan demanded a bribe, the person lodged a complaint with the DVAC officials. The DVAC arrested Pandiarajan when he received the bribe of Rs1,000 on July 11, 2008.In February 2018, the special court for trial of cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act in Madurai, convicted and sentenced Pandiarajan to two years imprisonment. Challenging the judgment, Pandiarajan preferred an appeal before HC. In May 2025, the HC modified the sentence to one year’s imprisonment and ordered Pandiarajan to be secured to undergo the sentence of imprisonment.The case was listed before the court under the caption ‘for reporting compliance’ on August 3. Justice K K Ramakrishnan observed that the court modified the sentence and ordered to sentence Pandiarajan in May 2025. Challenging the HC order, Pandiarajan preferred an appeal before the Supreme Court and the same was also dismissed in December 2025.The judge observed that despite the same, investigating officer Suriya Kala had not secured the accused to undergo the remaining period of imprisonment. Hence, the judge gave the direction to the chief vigilance commissioner to appear on August 10.
Article Summary: Madras HC summons vigilance officer over failure to imprison convicted VAO. P T M Pandiarajan was working as the VAO of Nadumuthalaikulam village in Madurai district. He was also in-charge of Panniyan, Kullaneri and Kannanur villages.

Article Title: HC orders desilting of Narasingam temple tank in six months
Article Text:
The Madras high court on Thursday directed the authorities to desilt the temple tank of the Yoga Narasimha Perumal Temple at Narasingam in Madurai district within six months.

Madurai

:





The Madras high court on Thursday directed the authorities to desilt the temple tank of the Yoga Narasimha Perumal Temple at Narasingam in Madurai district within six months.A division bench of Justice G R Swaminathan and Justice B Pugalendhi also directed the authorities to ensure that no garbage is dumped in or around the temple tank.The order was passed while disposing of a public interest litigation filed by J Kanagaraj of Madurai. The petitioner submitted that the ancient temple tank, located next to the historic rock-cut cave temple at Narasingam near Othakadai, had not been desilted for several years. As a result, it had become heavily silted and overgrown with bushes and weeds, while its retaining walls had deteriorated due to poor maintenance.He also alleged that garbage and plastic waste were being dumped in and around the tank, creating an unhygienic environment, affecting the sanctity of the temple premises and posing a health hazard to devotees.Recording the submissions, the bench directed the authorities to complete the desilting work within six months and ensure that no waste is dumped in or around the temple tank.
Article Summary: The Madras high court on Thursday directed the authorities to desilt the temple tank of the Yoga Narasimha Perumal Temple at Narasingam in Madurai district within six months. The order was passed while disposing of a public interest litigation filed by J Kanagaraj of Madurai. The petitioner submitted that the ancient temple tank had not been desilted for several years.

Article Title: Truck driver dies in road accident near Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A driver died in an accident involving a truck, a pickup van and a bus near Mecheri in Salem district on Wednesday. More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident.According to the Mecheri police, a TNSTC bus carrying 51 passengers was heading to Karur from Mettur when a speeding pickup van attempted to overtake it. “The pickup van collided head-on with a truck coming from the opposite direction,” said an officer at the Mecheri police station. The truck grazed the bus, shattering its windows and injuring more than 10 passengers seated near the windows.Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. The injured were rushed to govt hospitals in Mettur and Omalur.Fire service personnel, assisted by Mecheri police and residents, worked to move the damaged truck and pickup van to the roadside. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.The Mecheri police registered a case.
Article Summary: More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident. Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.

Article Title: Kochi police bust gang involved in nearly ₹1 crore fake-gold loan fraud
Article Text:
Kochi

:





The city police have arrested five people for allegedly defrauding a private financial firm in Palarivattom of nearly Rs 1 crore by pledging gold-plated imitation jewellery bearing hallmark stamps.According to Palarivattom Police, the fraud was allegedly carried out between June 13 and July 27, 2026. One of the accused, Vishnu of Kannur, initially pledged genuine gold ornaments on two occasions to gain confidence of the firm’s employees. He and his accomplices subsequently made several visits to the same branch and allegedly obtained loans by pledging fake ornaments carrying hallmark stamps.The fraud came to light during an internal audit. On July 29, Vishnu returned to the firm with his alleged accomplice Rahul of Wayanad, to pledge more ornaments. The employees then alerted Palarivattom police.Acting on a complaint from the branch manager, police registered a case and arrested the duo the same day. They were produced before a court and remanded in judicial custody.Police subsequently arrested Libin Xavier, 34, of Idukki, who allegedly supplied the ornaments and collected the proceeds, from Muvattupuzha area. Arshal Ismail, 32, of Idukki, who allegedly planned the fraud, and Shinoj, 42, of Kothamangalam, who allegedly manufactured gold-plated imitation ornaments and sold them to the other accused, were arrested from a hideout.The absconding accused were tracked down at different locations in Ernakulam.During raids, police seized ornaments allegedly used in the fraud, raw materials used in their manufacture, mobile phones regularly used by the gang and SIM cards obtained using fake addresses.The arrests were made by a special investigation team led by Ernakulam ACP K J Peter and Palarivattom inspector Anoop A. The team included SIs Jageesh R and Mithun Mohan, assistant SI Sighosh P V, and senior CPOs Aneesh N A, Jipinlal and Akhil Padman.All the arrested accused have been remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: The fraud was allegedly carried out between June 13 and July 27, 2026. One of the accused, Vishnu of Kannur, initially pledged genuine gold ornaments on two occasions to gain confidence of the firm’s employees. The fraud came to light during an internal audit.

Article Title: Explosives seizure: Kerala HC junks pre-arrest bail pleas of two accused persons
Article Text:
HC

Kochi

:





The high court has dismissed the pre-arrest bail petition filed by two accused, Mantagaud Biradar and Bapagaud Bheeramaya Choudri, in an NIA case arising from the seizure of a large cache of gelatin sticks and detonators at Tirurangadi in Malappuram.The petitioners are the proprietors of M/s Chetan Enterprises, a firm engaged in the business of explosives. They allegedly purchased the seized articles from M/s Vetrivel Explosives, Trichy, and transported them to Tirurangadi for supplying them to the first accused. While dismissing the petitions, the bench of Justices Sathish Ninan and P Krishna Kumar observed that the materials available in the case diary, prima facie, suggest that the petitioners, ninth and tenth accused, intentionally aided the first accused with full knowledge that he would use the explosives in unauthorised quarries.The case arose from an incident on Feb 7, in which the local police intercepted a truck parked within the compound of a hollow bricks manufacturing unit near Tirurangadi, acting on prior information that explosives were being transported in the vehicle. Upon inspection, the police found 35 boxes containing 10,500 non-electric detonators and 448 boxes containing 89,600 gelatin sticks inside the truck. The explosives and detonators were found concealed beneath 133 sacks of onions.The police arrested six accused and later handed over the case to the NIA, suspecting a larger conspiracy behind the incident.Earlier, the petitioners approached the special NIA court, Kochi, seeking pre-arrest bail, but their applications were denied, following which they moved the HC. The additional solicitor general, appearing for the NIA, vehemently opposed the petitions, contending that the concealment of the explosives beneath more than 100 sacks of onions and the removal of barcode labels to prevent the tracking of their movement clearly indicated the unlawful object of the petitioners, warranting a thorough investigation for which their custodial interrogation was indispensable. He further argued that the possibility of the explosives being intended for use in anti-national activities could not be ruled out. He also submitted that the petitioners are involved in several other criminal cases involving offences under the Explosive Substances Act.After perusing the case diary, the bench observed that, although it did not find any material at this stage indicating that the explosives were procured for use in anti-national activities, the materials available in the case diary, prima facie, suggest that the petitioners intentionally aided the first accused with full knowledge that he would use the explosives in unauthorised quarries. The bench further observed that the custodial interrogation of the petitioners appeared necessary for the effective progress of the investigation and, accordingly, dismissed the petitions.
Article Summary: The high court has dismissed the pre-arrest bail petition filed by two accused, Mantagaud Biradar and Bapagaud Bheeramaya Choudri. The case arose from the seizure of a large cache of gelatin sticks and detonators at Tirurangadi in Malappuram. The petitioners are the proprietors of M/s Chetan Enterprises, a firm engaged in the business of explosives.
